sentences.original: I rec^d^ yours of y^e^ 3^d^ Ult^o^ by the hand of M^r^ Blair, & it gave me more comfort than I can well expreſs.
sentences.modern: I received your letter of the 3rd of last month by the hand of Mr. Blair, and it gave me more comfort than I can well express.

sentences.original: We are hutted here for y^e^ Winter, & the Men ſuffer much for want of Shoes & Blankets.
sentences.modern: We are living in huts here for the winter, and the men suffer greatly for lack of shoes and blankets.

sentences.original: Gen^l^ Waſhington has wrote to Congreſs in the ſtrongeſt terms, & we hope for relief ere long.
sentences.modern: General Washington has written to Congress in the strongest terms, and we hope for relief before long.

sentences.original: Pray tell my Mother I am in good health, & kiſs the Children for me.
sentences.modern: Please tell my mother I am in good health, and kiss the children for me.

sentences.original: I ſhall write again by the firſt opportunity to Williamsburg.
sentences.modern: I shall write again at the first opportunity to Williamsburg.

sentences.original: I am, my dear Sarah, your moſt affectionate Husband Josiah Harwood
sentences.modern: I am, my dear Sarah, your most affectionate husband, Josiah Harwood

glossary.note: The 'y' stands for the old letter thorn (þ), pronounced 'th'.
Short for Latin 'ultimo', meaning last month.
The army built log huts for the winter encampment.
A polite way to make a request.
